scenes.title: The Poet's Freedom
scenes.summary: The poet imitates things as they were or are, as they are said to be, or as they ought to be, in a diction with its licenses. Errors of the art differ from incidental errors, like a horse with both right legs thrown forward.

scenes.title: Errors of Art and of Fact
scenes.summary: An impossibility is justified if it serves the end, like the pursuit of Hector; not knowing that a hind has no horns is a lesser fault than painting badly.

scenes.title: As They Ought to Be, as People Say
scenes.summary: Sophocles made people as they ought to be, Euripides as they are; the stories of the gods are what people say; the spears planted upright were the custom then, as among the Illyrians now; a deed must be judged by its agent, occasion and end.

scenes.title: Solutions from Language
scenes.summary: Rare words (the mules, Dolon's looks, "mix it stronger"), metaphor (all the gods slept), accent (Hippias of Thasos), punctuation (Empedocles), ambiguity (the night), and usage (tin greaves, Ganymede's wine).

scenes.title: Contradictions and Prejudice
scenes.summary: Consider every sense a word can bear, like the bronze spear stopped; do not judge the poet by one's own assumptions, as critics did over Icarius and Icadius.

scenes.title: The Twelve Solutions
scenes.summary: The impossible is defended by poetry, the better, or opinion, as Zeuxis painted; criticism is just when irrationality and baseness are needless, as Aegeus and Menelaus; five grounds of criticism, twelve solutions.

quotations.note: Not in our text of 2.15; compare 21.297.
Unattributed here; quoted as Agathon's at 1456a24–25.
